subject: Agriculture
title: Feed Conversion Ratios
description: A short lesson to help you apply Feed Conversion Ratios.

hook.text: It takes 8 kg of feed to produce 1 kg of beef—but only 2 kg of feed for 1 kg of chicken.

buildup.text: Feed conversion ratio measures how efficiently an animal turns plant calories into meat calories.

discovery.text: Chickens convert feed to meat four times more efficiently than cattle. Pigs fall in between.

twist.text: Fish are even better—some species achieve 1.2:1 ratios. Cold blood means less energy wasted on body heat.

climax.text: These ratios explain why chicken is cheap and beef expensive—and why aquaculture is booming.

punchline.text: The most efficient meat animal is one that doesn't waste energy staying warm.

quiz.question: Why are fish more feed-efficient than cattle?
options: Being cold-blooded, they waste less energy on body heat
